latest_events.title: Mali : les FAMa neutralisent une dizaine de terroristes
latest_events.summary: Les Forces armées maliennes (FAMa) ont annoncé avoir neutralisé au moins une dizaine de combattants terroristes et mis hors d’usage sept motocyclettes lors de frappes menées les 23 et 24 novembre dans plusieurs régions du pays, notamment dans le cadre de la traque des auteurs de l’attaque contre Niono. Dans un communiqué publié mardi, l’État-major général des Armées indique que ces interventions ont été conduites dans le cadre de l’opération Dougoukoloko, avec l’appui de partenaires, à travers des actions de surveillance, de reconnaissance et de frappes ciblées contre des positions de groupes armés.

latest_events.title: Expelled from Guinea: More than 1,100 people still present at the Bamako site
latest_events.summary: As part of the return operations, a lorry was mobilised on 16 November from the Kouremalé assembly site to transport around 110 people, including four to the Bamako District and 106 to Burkina Faso. On 17 November, the Burkinabé authorities also deployed 20 buses, two military trucks and 16 medical ambulances to ensure the care and return of their compatriots.

latest_events.title: The Malian Air Force receives new helicopters and a transport aircraft
latest_events.summary: On Monday, 16 November 2026, the President of Mali's Transitional Government, Army General Assimi Goïta, presided over a ceremony at Bamako's Président Modibo Keïta International Airport to hand over new aircraft to the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa). This delivery covers seven aircraft. These include four Mi-24 attack helicopters, two Mi-8 utility helicopters and one Ilyushin Il-76 strategic transport aircraft.

report_summaries.title: Mali: The army receives a new batch of aircraft
report_summaries.summary: Mali: The army takes delivery of a new batch of aircraft The Malian army is expanding its air fleet. On Monday, 16 November 2026, it took delivery of a new batch of aircraft on the tarmac of the presidential pavilion at Modibo Keita International Airport in Bamako. The Transitional President, Army General Assimi Goïta, presided over the ceremony in the presence of civil and military authorities.
